content: In children and adolescents diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, the consistent use of real-time continuous glucose monitoring (rtCGM) has been associated with significant improvements in blood glucose management. This often results in enhanced psychological well-being for both the patients and their families. Clinical trials have shown that rtCGM alleviates the stress associated with glucose management for young patients and their caregivers. This reduction in stress contributes to better adherence to prescribed diabetes management protocols. In adult patients, particularly those utilizing multiple daily injections (MDI) or continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII), rtCGM has been shown to significantly lower hemoglobin A1C levels by approximately 0.3% to 0.9%. Additionally, it has been effective in reducing the frequency of hypoglycemic episodes, indicating improved overall glycemic control.
